classification.difficultyReason: Construct each supplied line pair and connect equation rearrangements to the taught unique/parallel/coincident graphical cases.

content.prompt: For each pair of equations, draw the two straight lines and determine whether there are no solutions, one solution or infinitely many solutions.

answer.worked: For $y=2x+3$, plot $(-\tfrac32,0)$ and $(0,3)$. For $y=-x+3$, plot $(0,3)$ and $(3,0)$. Draw both lines through their plotted points. They intersect at $(0,3)$, so there is one solution.

spec.description: Complete solution graph with two equation-driven lines, coordinate intercepts and their common intersection. Dash distinguishes the second line.
spec.mathematics: The lines y=2x+3 and y=-x+3 intersect at (0,3).

answer.worked: Write the first equation as $y=-\tfrac12x+3$. Plot its intercepts $(0,3)$ and $(6,0)$. For $y=4x+3$, plot $(-\tfrac34,0)$ and $(0,3)$. Draw both lines. They intersect at $(0,3)$, so there is one solution.

spec.description: Complete solution graph showing both lines through (0,3), with their distinct x-intercepts.

answer.short: No solutions; the lines are parallel.
answer.worked: The second equation is $y=2x+3$. Plot $(-3,0)$ and $(0,6)$ for the first line, and $(-\tfrac32,0)$ and $(0,3)$ for the second. Both lines have gradient $2$, with different $y$-intercepts. Their graphs are parallel, so there are no solutions.

spec.description: Two parallel lines with all four source answer intercepts labelled.
spec.mathematics: Both gradients are 2; y-intercepts are 6 and 3.

answer.short: Infinitely many solutions; the lines coincide.
answer.worked: Rearranging $x+y=6$ gives $y=-x+6$, exactly the second equation. Plot $(0,6)$ and $(6,0)$ and draw the line through them. Both equations give this same line, so every point on it is a solution.

spec.description: One line representing both equations, with intercepts (0,6) and (6,0).

answer.short: No solutions; the lines are parallel.
answer.worked: Write the equations as $y=-x+6$ and $y=-x+8$. Draw the first line through $(0,6)$ and $(6,0)$, and the second through $(0,8)$ and $(8,0)$. The graphs have equal gradient $-1$ and different intercepts, so they are parallel and there are no solutions.

spec.description: Two parallel lines with intercept pairs (0,6), (6,0) and (0,8), (8,0).
spec.mathematics: Both gradients are -1, with distinct intercepts.

answer.short: Infinitely many solutions; the lines coincide.
